messages.content: What is the best month to visit Hawaii?

function.name: get_average_monthly_temperature

message.content:
The “best” month to visit Hawaii depends on what you’re looking for—weather, crowds, or price—but generally **April, May, September, and October** strike a great balance.

| What you want | Why it’s good |
|---------------|---------------|
| **Mild temperatures & lower humidity** | Late spring (April–May) and early fall (September–October) have comfortable daytime highs around 80 °F (27 °C) and cooler evenings. |
| **Fewer crowds & better deals** | These shoulder months see fewer tourists than peak summer (June–August) or holiday periods (December–January). |
| **Clear skies & good surf** | April–May often bring calmer seas and clearer skies, while September–October can still offer excellent surfing conditions before the winter swell starts. |
| **Wildlife viewing** | Early fall is prime whale‑watching season (especially in Maui), and the chance to spot humpback whales off the coast is high from November through March. |

If you’re after the absolute warmest weather and don’t mind crowds, **July and August** are the hottest months (average highs ~86 °F/30 °C) but also the most crowded and expensive. Conversely, **November–March** offers cooler temperatures (~75 °F/24 °C) and the best chances to see migrating humpback whales, though it’s also the wettest period.

So, if you want a mix of pleasant weather, fewer crowds, and reasonable prices, aim for **late spring or early fall**—April, May, September, or October.
